page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3442.17 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2532.0. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a gzip compression speed of 37.65 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression speed of 16.7 GB/sec. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall into the average tier, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 9797.0 and uncached large-block memory read speeds of 48.64 GB/sec.

While the instance excels in single-threaded execution and text processing, it exhibits performance limitations in complex workloads. For instance, LLM inference prompt processing with a medium 7B model is weak, registering at 30.28 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average at 11.21 tokens/sec. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lack of local storage, this instance is configured for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and standard database operations rather than heavy local storage-dependent or GPU-accelerated tasks.

It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The hardware configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU execution, single-threaded text processing, and gzip compression, while multi-core operations and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. A notable tradeoff is its weak prompt processing performance for medium-sized language models. This instance is configured for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and standard database operations that do not require local NVMe storage.
